channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Alexis Christoforous, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US and China Seek Common Ground on AI
item.description: Bloomberg News Chief North Asia Correspondent Stephen Engle and ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s summit highlighted efforts to establish dialogue on AI while building trust between the two countries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle and Kingston examine the significance of Xi’s state visit, China’s push to be treated as an equal to the US and the diplomatic signals surrounding the meetings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Syracuse's Semiconductor Gamble May Help Save the Rust Belt
item.description: What does it actually take to bring a Rust Belt city back to life? Micron is building one of the largest semiconductor factories in US history in Syracuse, a city that experienced major job loss after companies including GE, Carrier and General Motors left the area. Rob Simpson of CenterState CEO explains what attracted Micron to the city, local business owner Darin Price talks about what the investment means on the ground, and Brookings economist Joseph Parilla makes the case that Syracuse could be a model for reindustrialization across America. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Birding Apps Bring More People Into the Wild
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, writer and photographer Alexandra Marvar explains how apps such as Merlin are making birding easier and more accessible, helping draw new people to a hobby that offers an escape into nature. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Marvar also explores whether technology can remove some of the challenge, learning and satisfaction that traditionally come with identifying birds. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mexico Stresses Sovereignty in US Cooperation
item.description: Mexico’s foreign minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the country maintains a strong relationship with the US while insisting cooperation on security must respect Mexico’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, he says Mexico remains cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations as it seeks relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Ukraine War Becomes Economic Battle
item.description: New York Times Kyiv bureau chief Andrew Kramer tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia and Ukraine are increasingly targeting each other’s economies as the war shifts toward attacks on energy, transportation and export infrastructure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kramer says Ukraine is using its expanding drone arsenal to target Russia’s oil industry and its ability to finance a prolonged war. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: McDonald’s Selloff Hits 30% as Big Mac Inflation Spurs Pushback
item.description: McDonald’s Corp. faces a key challenge as it fights to reinvigorate a sagging stock price: Winning back the cost-conscious diners who believe its menu has become too expensive.
item.dc:creator: Peyton Forte

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: Campus Moms, smuggling butter, bringing iced coffee to a job interview, and the 'what's for dinner' question: Join Alexis Christoforous, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Higher Bond Yields Mark a Return to Normal
item.description: Ritholtz Wealth Management founder Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising bond yields reflect both a normalization of interest rates and inflationary pressures from factors including tariffs and higher energy prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz says higher yields have made fixed income more attractive while investors should consider whether strong equity gains have pushed their portfolios away from their intended allocations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Northeast Faces Wind, Rain and Coastal Flooding
item.description: Bloomberg News meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nor'easter will bring waves of heavy rain and strong winds to the Northeast, along with risks from falling trees, localized flooding and dangerous coastal conditions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says coastal flooding could affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut and Massachusetts as rough ocean conditions persist through multiple high-tide cycles. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
item.description: Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The China Trade Problem That Tariffs Alone Can't Fix
item.description: China ran a $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, many of its companies don't need to make a profit, and its exports are growing at two to three times the rate of the global economy. Michael Froman, former US Trade Representative under President Obama and now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, tells us why Xi Jinping sees a consumer-led economy as a political threat, and what happens when China finally runs out of countries willing to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Xi Summit Leaves Big Issues Unresolved
item.description: Bloomberg North Asia correspondent Stephen Engle tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping bought more time to negotiate over trade while major disagreements involving Taiwan, Iran and technology remain. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle explains how competition over AI and unresolved economic and security issues are shaping the next phase of US-China relations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit Yields Coal Pledge as Tariff Talks Extend
item.description: China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US next year and again in 2028, according to the White House, in a sign of progress in easing trade frictions.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Billionaire Charoen’s Asset World Targets $1 Billion REIT IPO
item.description: Asset World Corp Pcl’s new Thai Real Estate Investment Trust aims to raise at least $1 billion through a listing as it seeks funds to expand its hotel and commercial property business, according to a senior executive.
item.dc:creator: Anuchit Nguyen

item.title: Blackstone Cements Shift From Star Dealmakers With Baratta Exit
item.description: If there was any doubt that Jon Gray is now the center of gravity at Blackstone Inc., the past few weeks have erased it.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Singh and Dawn Lim

item.title: Wall Street Week | China’s Trade Reckoning, Syracuse’s Second Chance, Humanoids in Healthcare
item.description: This week, Council on Foreign Relations President Michael Froman breaks down China's export machine, why twenty years of US pressure hasn't worked, and what happens next. And, can a $100 billion Micron factory transform Syracuse from a Rust Belt cautionary tale into a potential model for American reindustrialization? Plus, a bridge named for a hockey legend was meant to strengthen the supply chain between the US and Canada, but the neighbors can’t agree on their trade relationship. Later, with 760,000 care aide openings expected every year in the US and a $400 billion long-term care bill, humanoid robots are an early bet on technology filling the care gap. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ellison Pledges $9.2 Billion More in Oracle Shares for Loans
item.description: Larry Ellison, a key figure behind Paramount Skydance Corp.’s deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., has pledged 67 million more shares of Oracle Corp. as collateral for personal loans than he had at the same time last year.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Palmeri and Brody Ford

item.title: SK Hynix’s Solidigm Is Said to Weigh US IPO as Soon as 2027
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s Solidigm is considering a US initial public offering as soon as next year, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz

item.title: David Booth on Investing, Dimensional and Staying Calm | The David Rubenstein Show
item.description: David Booth started Dimensional Fund Advisors out of a Brooklyn brownstone in 1981 with an idea that challenged conventional investing: investors should have exposure to smaller companies as part of a diversified portfolio. Today, Dimensional manages more than $1 trillion. Booth sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss his new book, "Stay Calm," which applies his investment philosophy of staying calm during periods of market volatility, to navigating the uncertainties of life. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded August 10 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
